issue.body:
Pin what goes into a query and what comes out: the zod spec generated from the registry, its one canonical spelling in links and short codes, and the result shapes with the agent cap.

## What's in it

- query/spec.ts: querySpec is a zod union on the dataset, generated from the registry with one filter variant per column, and v must be 1. It is as exact as the registry allows; what an agent tool publishes is #50's choice. It uses Honeycomb's field names, allows at most 10 calculations, 20 filters, 3 breakdowns, and 10 havings and a limit up to 1,000, and rejects any named granularity finer than the dataset's grain, which each registry dataset declares. A spec without a granularity asks for totals only. A query covers at most 3,660 nights, and each granularity fewer (2s: 1, 30s: 7, 1m: 14, 5m: 31, 15m: 92, 1h: 366), so a fine step over a long range is refused. granularity can also be "auto": the finest allowed step that gives one group at most 300 buckets, which depends only on the spec. granularityOf(dataset, spec) resolves it
- COUNT takes no column, COUNT_DISTINCT takes any, SUM, AVG, and the percentiles take a metric, and MIN and MAX take any number, integer, timestamp, or date column and give that kind
- nights is {last: n} or {from, to}. Dates and times are ISO text, and a time carries its offset. Filter values are typed per column and given in display units. parseSpec returns the spec with every default filled in. Cross-field checks cover calculation kinds, groupable breakdowns, orders and havings that refer to the spec, and IN-list caps. Errors name the field path and the allowed values
- A registry-driven fast-check arbitrary for valid specs, shared with the query engine
- query/canonical.ts fixes the key order, drops defaults, sorts and dedupes IN lists, writes times in UTC, and writes a repeated filter or having once. Clauses keep their written order. query/link.ts builds and parses /explore?q= with the 4,000-character cap, and a failed parse keeps the raw text for the error view
- query/short-code.ts derives a ten-character lower-case Crockford base32 code from SHA-256 (WebCrypto) over canonical JSON tagged with its kind, so a spec and a SQL text never share a code
- api/query.ts, api/sql.ts, and api/agent.ts define QueryResult (columns, groups with whole-range totals, and, when the spec has a granularity, series: {granularity, rows}, with the step used and flat rows of {bucket, group, values}), SqlResult with the 10,000-row web cap, and the compact agent result: {columns, rows as arrays, truncated, link, short_link, hint}
- capForAgent(rows, budget) keeps at most 200 rows or the given character budget, whichever runs out first, and sets truncated and the hint. MCP tools and finding snapshots share it

## Tests

- A table of accepted and rejected specs (11 calculations, > on an enum, an unknown value, an ungroupable breakdown, an order on a missing calculation, 2s on nights, v: 2), and every spec from the arbitrary parses
- fast-check: canonicalize is idempotent and ignores key order, and parsing toExploreUrl(spec) returns canonicalize(spec). Golden short codes for three fixed specs
- capForAgent cuts at row 200, cuts earlier when the budget runs out, never splits a row, and leaves a short result alone
